slot.brief: letter-shift code: a word is coded by shifting each letter by a constant value or reversing position; apply the same rule to decode/coding a new word

stem: In a certain code language, **TIGER** is written as **WLJHU**. How will **HORSE** be written in that language?
working: Rule: each letter moves 3 steps forward in the alphabet (T->W, I->L, G->J, E->H, R->U). Applying +3 to HORSE: H->K, O->R, S->V, E->H, R->U, giving KRUVH. B swaps the last two letters, C shifts O->S instead of O->R, and D shifts E->W instead of E->H, so none of them follows the constant +3 rule.
solution: Each letter is shifted 3 places forward in the alphabet: $H\to K$, $O\to R$, $R\to U$, $S\to V$, $E\to H$. Thus, $\text{HORSE}\to\text{KRUHV}$.
